meta.method: Each official page was opened again with the web reader on 2026-11-13. For each ledger row listed, every number in the row's value that was re-read is checked to appear in the text recorded here, copied from the page. Numbers in a value that were not re-read are listed as not_reread. No ledger value was changed by this record.
meta.rule: canonical/verify.py check 12 re-tests every confirmed number against the ledger value and this text.

entries.note: The page posts the 11/10/2026 row (10-year 4.98), the 11/12/2026 row (5.10) and the 11/13/2026 row (5.15). The model's reinvestment anchor (CM-001) was moved on the access date by session 575eebba from the 11/10/2026 row to the 11/13/2026 row, so CM-001 and CM-008 now hold the same 11/13/2026 value. The earlier base case used 4.98, the 11/10/2026 value.

entries.read_text: Note: Effective for transactions closing after June 30, 2026, the new ULA thresholds will be $5,400,000 and $10,900,000. Transactions greater than $5,400,000 but less than $10,900,000 will be assessed a 4% tax, and transactions of $10,900,000 or greater will be assessed a 5.5% tax.
entries.note: The page's rate table also gives 0.45% for sales up to $5,400,000 (base tax only). The city-plus-county figure in TX-015 is a computed row and was not re-derived here.

entries.read_text: [table cells in order] Population estimates, July 1, 2025, (V2025) | 3,869,089 | 9,694,934 | Population, percent change - April 1, 2020 (estimates base) to July 1, 2025, (V2025) | -0.8% | -3.2%
entries.note: The QuickFacts page lists Los Angeles city and Los Angeles County, both Vintage 2025 estimates. Its population-change line gives -3.2% for the county.
The 2026 table lists one change so far: the September 17, 2026 increase of 25 basis points. No later 2026 meeting is listed on the page on 2026-11-13.

entries.read_text: Same-store sales declined 1.1% in the third quarter, comprised of franchise same-store sales decline of 1.2% and company-owned same-store sales decline of 0.9%. [table] System | (1.1 %)
entries.note: The restaurant counts behind TN-085 (2,115 at July 5, 2026 and 2,168 a year earlier) also appear on this release. TN-085 is a computed row and was not recomputed here.

entries.read_text: Closed on $221.7 million of investments at an initial cash cap rate of 7.3%, with a weighted average lease term of 19.6 years
entries.note: This is the national net-lease cap rate for NNN REIT's own acquisitions. It is one buyer's pricing, not a market survey.

entries.read_text: [table cells in order] Los Angeles region | Magnitude (greater than or equal to) | Average repeat time (years) | 30-year likelihood of one or more events | Readiness | 6.7 | 40 | (2.1) | 60% (0.8) | 1.1
entries.note: Table 1 of the fact sheet, which gives the 30-year likelihood counted from 2014. The fact sheet is from 2015; it is the official UCERF3 forecast and has not been replaced by a newer official table in this review.

entries.read_text: Accommodation and food services (up 8,600) boosted the employment levels, with additions mainly centered in restaurants and other eating places (up 7,300).
entries.note: The 7,300 figure matches. The 2.1% share in the ledger value is in the release's table, which was not re-read in this pass, so it is listed as not re-read.

entries.read_text: The biggest decline in enrollment is expected in Los Angeles County, which will fall by 240,800 students by the end of the 10-year projection.
entries.note: The page states a fall of 240,800 students. The ledger computes -19.4% from two spreadsheet operands (1,002,045 and 1,242,816). Their difference, 240,771, rounds to the page's 240,800. The operands are in the Department of Finance spreadsheet, which was not re-opened in this pass, so the -19.4% is not re-confirmed today.

sensitivity.test: The model was run in a temporary copy twice: with the reinvestment anchor at 4.98 (the 11/10/2026 value, the earlier base case) and at 5.15 (the 11/13/2026 value, the anchor now on main). The repository was not changed.
sensitivity.score_change_range: going from 4.98 to 5.15 raises every strategy's pooled balanced score, by between 21 and 58 points (sell now and hold the proceeds in Treasuries: about 58; sell through an exchange: about 21)
